messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw two OOMs on canary with continuous-batching + kernel-switch enabled. Happened during high-concurrency chat load. Dumped allocator watermarks and KV cache stats. Repro steps below.

sam: thanks, can you paste the allocator log and the batch shape distribution?

maya: paste below. quick summary: batch growth from 8->23 seqs over ~200ms, padding jumped, workspace high-water at 20.9Gi, then kernel swap caused a transient workspace resize and immediate OOM.

maya: ```
Allocator snapshot:
  total_reserved: 24.0 GiB
  total_used: 21.9 GiB
  workspace_high: 20.9 GiB
  slab_frag: 1.12 GiB
  pads: 3.3 GiB
KV cache: entries=1874, kv_size=4.1 GiB, per_seq_kv_avg=2.2 MiB
Batch shapes last 10s: [8,9,10,12,18,23,23,20,15,9]
Stack: kernel_switch -> workspace_resize -> cudaMalloc -> OOM
```

ryan: interesting — kernel_switch -> workspace_resize pattern is new after the kernel-selection change. Means we try a different matmul kernel path which adjusts per-op workspace estimates at runtime. If batch grows fast, workspace estimate increases but memory accounting lags and allocator reserves too late./cc @li

li: ok that matches my local runs. I saw pad amplification when sequences spawn mid-batch: per-seq pad goes from ~4 KiB -> 22 KiB when we align to 64B boundaries for the new kernel. That alone explains ~1.2GiB extra padding for 18+ sequences.

ryan: profiling output: 
```
Perf counters (canary-2026-03-):
  matmul_kernel: switch_count=4
  avg_workspace_per_op: 48.6 MiB -> 74.1 MiB after switch
  memory_accounting_lag: 90ms median, 320ms p95
```

sam: so two contributors: (1) kernel path increases per-op workspace, (2) batch growth + pad alignment increases aggregate padding, (3) accounting lag doesn't reserve early enough.

maya: yes. Also saw KV cache reclaim did not trigger because pressure check used reserved (not used) memory; reclaim threshold looks at free reservation, which didn't dip until after cudaMalloc failed.

alloc-bot: Note: auto-reclaim triggered but failed due to racing allocs. Thresholds: reclaim when used_ratio>0.78 and reservation_free<2 GiB.

ryan: propose short-term mitigation: reduce workspace_max_percent on kernel-switch to cap speculative increase, and change reclaim check to use used_mem (not reserved) for pressure signal. Also tighten pad alignment for the new kernel to 16B if safe.

li: I can land pad alignment patch and add a safe fallback to 64B only for NV kernels that actually require it. I have a microbenchmark showing negligible perf delta with 16B in most ranges.

sam: i'll open a canary patch to: 
- lower workspace_max_percent from 0.85 -> 0.7 for kernel-switch path
- change reclaim metric to used_mem/reserved_total
- add early async reclaim (start reclaim at memory_accounting_lag p50)

maya: ACTIONS
- li: pad alignment patch + bench (ETA today)
- ryan: change reclaim metric + unit tests (ETA tomorrow)
- sam: canary config & rollout (ETA today afternoon)
- maya: collect more logs during canary (I will enable detailed mem telemetry)

li: quick note — we should also look at per-seq KV overhead when sequences spawn mid-batch vs new request; I suspect we reserialize some kv blocks and double-count transiently. I'll add instrumentation.

maya: thanks. if we can get the pad fix + reclaim change in a canary before EOD we should avoid more OOM spikes.

sam: creating PR #2987 and canary config now. link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/2987 :rocket:

ryan: adding a regression test to simulate rapid batch growth by enqueuing spikes with 50ms inter-arrival. Will run overnight.

alloc-bot: Monitoring rule created: if OOM rate > 0.5/hour on canary -> rollback canary.

maya: nice. will post post-mortem if we see further events. thanks team :thumbsup:
